misconceptions.description: Reporting feelings, energy, or general engagement as if they were evidence of learning
misconceptions.trigger: reflection says the lesson went well or students were engaged with no observed data
misconceptions.feedback: Cite specific observed evidence such as scores, work samples, or subgroup results, not impressions.

misconceptions.description: Reporting only evidence that supports the preferred conclusion and ignoring counter-evidence
misconceptions.trigger: reflection lists supporting data but no disconfirming observation
misconceptions.feedback: Actively report what you saw that argued against your conclusion before deciding.

misconceptions.description: Letting AI write a reflection it cannot ground in observed classroom evidence
misconceptions.trigger: reflection on the teacher's own lesson is generated wholesale by a model
misconceptions.feedback: Write from your own observed evidence; use AI only to question your reasoning, not to supply the observations.

misconceptions.description: Attributing an outcome to the tool because they co-occurred, without checking rival explanations
misconceptions.trigger: reflection credits the tool for a gain that has obvious alternative causes
misconceptions.feedback: List and rule out rival explanations before attributing the outcome to the tool.
